prompt.context_jp: ひとしきり時間が過ぎたあと、高野の携帯電話＿低く震えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 高野の携帯電話＿低く震えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits when a new event suddenly occurs in the narrative.

feedback.correct_en: The phone vibrating is a new event entering the scene — this 'sudden happening' reading takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the phone as a pre-established topic, but here the ringing is fresh news the reader learns.

contrast_examples.jp: その電話は高野のだった。
contrast_examples.en: That phone was Takano's. (now it's the topic)

prompt.context_jp: 画面に表示されていたのは、…二ツ木の名前だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 画面に表示されていたの＿、二ツ木の名前だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for the 'the X was Y' identification pattern.

feedback.correct_en: '〜のは…だった' is a cleft that presents the displayed thing as the topic, with the name given as the new info. The topic slot takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here would wrongly pack the whole noun as new information, breaking the cleft structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 画面に表示されていたのは名前だ。
contrast_examples.en: What was displayed was a name. (cleft, topic は)

contrast_examples.jp: 画面に名前が表示された。
contrast_examples.en: A name was displayed on the screen. (new-info が)

prompt.context_jp: 蛍は畳の上に座り込み、昼間の出来事を何度も頭の中で巻き戻していた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蛍＿畳の上に座り込み、昼間の出来事を何度も頭の中で巻き戻していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle fitting a familiar character as the ongoing topic.

feedback.correct_en: Hotaru is already established as a main character; the sentence describes what she (as topic) is doing. は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight her as newly-noticed information, which doesn't match this introspective scene about an already-known character.

prompt.context_jp: 嬉しいはずなのに、なぜか胸のどこか＿ざらついている。
prompt.prompt_jp: なぜか胸のどこか＿ざらついている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces the unexpected sensation?

feedback.correct_en: The 'rough feeling somewhere in her chest' is newly-noticed internal information — a classic が subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the rough feeling is already an ongoing topic; here it's a fresh realization.

contrast_examples.en: Something feels off in my chest. (new sensation)

contrast_examples.jp: その違和感は消えない。
contrast_examples.en: That discomfort won't go away. (already topicalized)

prompt.context_jp: 部屋には扇風機の回る音だけ＿、やけに大きく響いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 扇風機の回る音だけ＿、やけに大きく響いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits '〜だけ' as the exclusive/only source?

feedback.correct_en: '〜だけが' marks exhaustive identification — only the fan sound and nothing else. This is the exhaustive-listing が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は after だけ would be unnatural here; we want to point out that this is the one and only thing audible.

contrast_examples.en: You're the only one I can rely on.
You, as for you, are reliable. (topic reading)

prompt.context_jp: 沈黙に耐えかねたように、蛍＿先に口を開いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蛍＿先に口を開いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Who spoke first? Pick the particle that highlights the actor.

feedback.correct_en: '〜が先に口を開いた' identifies which of the two people acted — exhaustive/new-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 蛍は would describe Hotaru as topic ('as for Hotaru…'), losing the nuance of 'it was Hotaru who went first'.

contrast_examples.en: It was Hotaru who spoke first.

prompt.context_jp: 決めたことをきちんと守るのはたいてい高野のほうで、蛍＿その隙間をすり抜けるのが得意だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蛍＿その隙間をすり抜けるのが得意だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that creates a contrast between Takano and Hotaru.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence sets up Takano vs. Hotaru — contrastive は marks the second half of this comparison.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply present her as the new subject, losing the 'in contrast' feel the sentence builds.

contrast_examples.jp: 兄はまじめだが、弟はなまけ者だ。
contrast_examples.en: The brother is diligent, but the younger one is lazy. (contrast)
It's the younger brother who's lazy. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: いいも何も、手嶋さん＿ただの同僚です。
prompt.prompt_jp: 手嶋さん＿ただの同僚です。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits defining 'Teshima-san' as just a colleague?

feedback.correct_en: 'XはYです' is the classic topic-description frame — Hotaru labels Teshima as 'just a colleague'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would wrongly read as 'It's Teshima who's just a colleague' (identifying which colleague), not describing him.

contrast_examples.jp: ただの友人なのは彼だ。
contrast_examples.en: The one who's just a friend is him. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: 好きな人と 2人きり＿されたんですよ!?
prompt.prompt_jp: 好きな人と 2人きり＿されたんですよ!?
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle marking the resulting state in '～にされる'.

feedback.correct_en: '〜にされる' means 'be made into/put into [state]'. Being 'left alone with him' is the resulting state marked by に.
feedback.incorrect_en: を or が don't mark the resulting state here; they'd break the 'be made [state]' structure.

prompt.context_jp: その一言＿、蛍の中で張りつめていた何か＿ぷつりと断ち切った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蛍の中で張りつめていた何か＿ぷつりと断ち切った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the 'something' as new info being revealed?

feedback.correct_en: '断ち切った' is transitive — 'cut off something'. The 'something' inside her is the direct object, marked by を.
feedback.incorrect_en: は or が would mark it as subject, but the sentence has 'その一言が' as the subject severing 'something' (object).

prompt.context_jp: だって 私＿ まだ好きだから！
prompt.prompt_jp: 私＿ まだ好きだから！
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle frames Hotaru's confession as a personal statement?

feedback.correct_en: She's talking about her own feelings as the topic/theme of the utterance — 私は + predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私が would turn it into 'I'm the one who still likes him' (identifying who), which isn't her point.

contrast_examples.en: I still love him. (my feelings as topic)
The one who loves him is me. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: 縁側の風鈴＿、張りつめた空気の中で一度だけ小さく鳴った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 縁側の風鈴＿、…一度だけ小さく鳴った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for a sudden single event in the scene?

feedback.correct_en: The wind chime ringing is a sudden, perceivable event — が presents it as fresh sensory info.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the wind chime a topic being described, draining the moment of its startling, one-off feel.

contrast_examples.en: The wind chime is a summer sound. (topic/description)

prompt.context_jp: 招待客たち＿いっせいに立ち上がり、口々に祝福の声をかけた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 招待客たち＿いっせいに立ち上がり、…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle treats the guests as the overall topic of this scene-description?

feedback.correct_en: The guests are the already-present group in the scene; the sentence describes what they (as a topic) did. は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight them as newly-noticed, as if just appearing — but they've been in the hall all along.

prompt.context_jp: とことん 自分の気持＿向き合って とことん ぶつかって行きゃええんよ｡
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の気持＿向き合って…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle goes with '向き合う' here?

feedback.correct_en: '〜に向き合う' = 'face up to ~'. The thing you face takes に, not を.
feedback.incorrect_en: を向き合う is ungrammatical; 向き合う is intransitive and takes に for its target.

contrast_examples.en: Tackle a problem. (に with similar verbs)

prompt.context_jp: 新聞を広げていた高野＿、その変わりように思わず目を上げた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 新聞を広げていた高野＿、その変わりように思わず目を上げた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for Takano, a known character reacting?

feedback.correct_en: Takano is the established character; the sentence describes his reaction as the topic-holder. は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly introduce him as new info, but he's been present throughout the scene.

prompt.context_jp: いくら考えても答え＿出ない。
prompt.prompt_jp: いくら考えても答え＿出ない。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for 'an answer won't come'.

feedback.correct_en: '答えが出ない' — 'an answer doesn't come out' is a fixed pattern where the answer is the new element with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 答えは出ない would contrastively mean 'as for an answer, it won't come', implying 'but something else does' — not the meaning here.

contrast_examples.jp: 答えは出ないが、ヒントは見える。
contrast_examples.en: The answer won't come, but hints do. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 本当＿、部長の前であんなふうに強がるつもりなどなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 本当＿、部長の前であんなふうに強がるつもりなどなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits '本当＿' as a topicalized preface?

feedback.correct_en: '本当は' = 'as for the truth / actually' — a common topic-marker use to frame what follows.
feedback.incorrect_en: 本当が doesn't form this adverbial 'actually/to tell the truth' expression.

contrast_examples.en: Actually, I don't want to go.
Tell the truth. (object use of の)

prompt.context_jp: 互いに詮索するつもりはないという顔をしながら、相手の様子を＿うかがっている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 相手の様子を＿うかがっている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which expression means 'watching out of the corner of one's eye'?

feedback.correct_en: '横目でうかがう' = glance sideways/out of the corner of the eye — the set collocation for secretly observing.
feedback.incorrect_en: '両目で' (both eyes) would mean openly looking; '片手で' (one hand) is nonsensical with 'うかがう'.

prompt.context_jp: そんな私が 恋をするわけ ないじゃないですか｡ あり得ません ＿で茶を沸かしますよ｡
prompt.prompt_jp: ＿で茶を沸かしますよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill the blank in this idiom meaning 'ridiculous / laughable'.

feedback.correct_en: 'へそで茶を沸かす' (brew tea with one's navel) is a set idiom for something absurdly funny or ridiculous.
feedback.incorrect_en: The idiom specifically uses へそ — no other body part works; it's a fixed expression.

contrast_examples.jp: へそで茶を沸かすような話。

prompt.context_jp: ＿な彼は、集積所に置く前に必ず袋の中身を確かめることにしている。
prompt.prompt_jp: ＿な彼は、必ず袋の中身を確かめることにしている。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the adjective that describes Takano's meticulous nature.

feedback.correct_en: '几帳面' = meticulous/precise, matching Takano's habit of checking everything carefully.
feedback.incorrect_en: '大ざっぱ' (sloppy) and 'のんき' (easygoing) are the opposite — they'd contradict the behavior described.

prompt.context_jp: 失敗して 手嶋さんに ＿がないんです！
prompt.prompt_jp: 手嶋さんに ＿がないんです！
prompt.prompt_en: Fill the idiom meaning 'can't face someone (out of shame)'.

feedback.correct_en: '〜に合わせる顔がない' is the fixed idiom for being too ashamed to face someone.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other phrasings aren't idiomatic — only '合わせる顔がない' carries the shame nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 両親に合わせる顔がない。
恥ずかしくて会えない。

prompt.context_jp: 思いは 言葉に＿ 伝わりません。
prompt.prompt_jp: 思いは 言葉に＿ 伝わりません。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb form that completes 'unless you put feelings into words'.

feedback.correct_en: '言葉にする' = 'put into words'. The conditional 'しなければ' means 'unless you do so'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'なければ' misses the する; 'するなら' flips the logic to 'if you do', which doesn't fit '伝わりません'.

contrast_examples.jp: 言葉にしなければ伝わらない。
contrast_examples.en: Unless you put it in words, it won't come across.
If you put it in words, it comes across.

prompt.context_jp: そのとき、何か大事なことを忘れているような気がして、彼女はぴたりと足を＿。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女はぴたりと足を＿。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb meaning 'stopped in her tracks'.

feedback.correct_en: '足を止める' is the fixed collocation for 'come to a stop while walking'.
feedback.incorrect_en: '足を置く' (put the foot down) and '足を引く' (pull back / withdraw) don't express 'halt mid-walk'.

prompt.context_jp: 迷いに迷った末にようやく＿決心が、足元からぐらぐらと揺らいでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ようやく＿決心が、…
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb best collocates with '決心'?

feedback.correct_en: '決心を固める' = firm up one's resolve — the standard collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: '決心を作る/置く' aren't natural Japanese; only '固める' (and '決める') pair with 決心.

prompt.context_jp: このまま胸の内にしまっておけるほど、蛍は＿人間でもない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蛍は＿人間でもない。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the adjective meaning 'skillful/clever' (at hiding feelings).

feedback.correct_en: '器用' here means skilled/adroit — Hotaru isn't the type who can skillfully bottle things up.
feedback.incorrect_en: '元気' (energetic) and '大切' (important) don't fit the sense of 'adeptly handling one's emotions'.

prompt.context_jp: 蛍が怒って高野を問い詰める場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: どちらが怒鳴り声として自然ですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as Hotaru angrily confronting her boss?

choices.text: どういうつもりですか！ 会議室に 鍵をかけて 閉じ込めるなんて、それが上司のすることですか！？
どういうおつもりでいらっしゃいますか。会議室に鍵をおかけになって閉じ込められるとは、上司としていかがなものかと存じます。

feedback.correct_en: A is punchy '〜ですか！' — natural for a subordinate venting anger. It keeps politeness (です) but loses the stiff keigo.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's heavy sonkeigo ('おつもりでいらっしゃいますか') is absurdly formal for an angry outburst at home — it undercuts the emotion.

contrast_examples.jp: ふざけないでください！
contrast_examples.en: Don't mess with me! (natural anger in です-form)

contrast_examples.jp: お戯れがすぎるのではないかと存じます。
contrast_examples.en: I believe your jest exceeds propriety. (unnaturally stiff)

prompt.context_jp: 山田が蛍を励ますセリフとして自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_jp: どちらがより自然ですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for Yamada's remark?

choices.text: うまく行かないから 恋愛って面白いんだけどね。
恋愛って面白いんだけどね、うまく行かないから。

feedback.correct_en: A puts the reason first ('because it doesn't go well') and the main point at the end — natural Japanese information flow.
feedback.incorrect_en: B tacks the reason on after the end-of-sentence ね, which sounds like an afterthought in writing/scripted speech.

prompt.context_jp: 蛍が上司・高野に報告するセリフとして自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_jp: どちらが同居人の上司への話し方として自然ですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which feels more natural as Hotaru telling her boss-roommate?

choices.text: 実は 私… 手嶋さんと… 普通の会話ができたんです！
実は俺、手嶋と普通の会話できたぜ！

feedback.correct_en: A uses 私 + です form — appropriate for a female character speaking to her boss, even in a casual home setting.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses 俺/ぜ — male rough speech that doesn't match Hotaru's voice or the subordinate-to-boss relationship.

contrast_examples.en: I managed to do it! (polite, excited)

prompt.context_jp: 現場での対応を伝える発話として自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_jp: どちらがより自然ですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural?

choices.text: 応急処置になるけど、朝までに現場は私のほうで何とかするから！
応急処置にはなるけど、朝まで現場を私で何とかしてるから！

feedback.correct_en: A uses the natural collocations '〜のほうで何とかする' (I'll handle it on my end) and '朝までに' (by morning — deadline).
feedback.incorrect_en: B's '私で何とかしてる' is ungrammatical, and '朝まで' means 'until morning' (duration), losing the deadline sense.

prompt.context_jp: 神宮司は広島弁話者。自然な彼のセリフは？
prompt.prompt_jp: 神宮司のセリフとして自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds right for Jinguji, who speaks Hiroshima dialect?

choices.text: せっかくの休みなんじゃけぇ、何もせんでのんびりする選択はないんかのう。
せっかくの休日ですので、何もせずのんびりする選択肢はございませんでしょうか。

feedback.correct_en: A uses Hiroshima-ben markers (じゃけぇ, せん, のう) that match Jinguji's established speech style.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is business-level keigo — totally out of character for Jinguji's rough regional speech to a close colleague.
